55.title: Installing the Breed bootloader
55.titles: Linksys EA7XXX › Installing from stock firmware
55.text: Installing OpenWrt Install OpenWrt for your device as described on the official website. Saving the calibration Save EEPROM/factory/mtd2 from your device. Installing the package Give the router internet access and install the kmod-mtd-rw package. Writing the bootloader Open a console and connect to the router over SSH. Serve breed.bin with HFS and run the commands: Enter one command at a time 1 cd /tmp 2 wget http://192.168.1.2/breed.bin 3 insmod mtd-rw i_want_a_brick= 1 4 mtd unlock /dev/mtd0 5 mtd write /tmp/breed.bin boot 6 reboot Backup Open Breed at 192.168.1.1 and save a Full dump backup in case you want to return to the factory firmware.

56.title: Flashing through Breed
56.titles: Linksys EA7XXX › Installing from stock firmware
56.text: Serving the files Start HFS and put all files from the archive into it, along with your calibration (EEPROM/factory/mtd2 ). The correct MAC addresses must be written into the calibration beforehand with the EEPROM tools. Flashing over Telnet Start PuTTY, connect over Telnet to 192.168.1.1 on port 23 and paste the commands with the right mouse button, waiting for the previous one to finish. Warning Turn off your OS firewall and antivirus beforehand. The messages skipped bad blocks and Flash erasure failed with -5 after entering the commands are normal. Caution Each line is a separate command. If it fails, run it again. Compare the IP in the wget commands below with the IP shown in HFS. In the Breed bootloader it always starts with 192.168.1.xxx. Enter one command at a time 1 flash erase 0x80000 0x7f00000 2 wget http://192.168.1.2/u-config.bin 3 flash write 0x80000 0x80001000 0x80000 4 flash write 0x4040000 0x80001000 0x80000 5 wget http://192.168.1.2/eeprom.bin 6 flash write 0x100000 0x80001000 0x80000 7 flash write 0x40c0000 0x80001000 0x80000 8 wget http://192.168.1.2/firmware.bin 9 flash write 0x180000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 10 flash write 0x4140000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 11 wget http://192.168.1.2/u-state.bin 12 flash write 0x3fc0000 0x80001000 0x80000 13 env set autoboot.command " boot flash 0x4140000 " 14 env save 15 reset Sample console output After the reboot the device starts Done! Router access Web interface 192.168.1.1 Wi-Fi password 12345678

214.title: Method II Old
214.titles: Xiaomi Router 4 › Installing from stock firmware
214.text: Serving the files Start !HFS.exe and drag all .bin files from the firmware folder: U-Config, U-State, EEPROM and Xiaomi4_xxx into its window. Tip To minimize installation problems, it is recommended to set the IP address 192.168.1.2 on the network card. Flashing over Telnet Start PuTTY, connect over Telnet to 192.168.1.1 on port 23 and paste the commands with the right mouse button, waiting for the previous one to finish. Warning Turn off your OS firewall and antivirus beforehand. The messages skipped bad blocks and Flash erasure failed with -5 after entering the commands are normal. Caution Each line is a separate command. If it fails, run it again. Compare the IP in the wget commands below with the IP shown in HFS. In the Breed bootloader it always starts with 192.168.1.xxx. Enter one command at a time 1 flash erase 0x80000 0x7f00000 2 wget http://192.168.1.2/u-config.bin 3 flash write 0x80000 0x80001000 0x80000 4 flash write 0x4040000 0x80001000 0x80000 5 wget http://192.168.1.2/eeprom.bin 6 flash write 0x100000 0x80001000 0x80000 7 flash write 0x40c0000 0x80001000 0x80000 8 wget http://192.168.1.2/firmware.bin 9 flash write 0x180000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 10 flash write 0x4140000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 11 wget http://192.168.1.2/u-state.bin 12 flash write 0x3fc0000 0x80001000 0x80000 13 env set autoboot.command " boot flash 0x4140000 " 14 env save 15 reset Sample console output How to make sure everything was flashed correctly The Settings section shows the device's service data (it is enough that it is there; some fields may differ). The MAC address section shows your MAC address from the device label or the one you entered in the converter (it may differ by ±1 in the last character). After the reboot the device starts. Done! 262.title: Method I
262.text: Power off the router, hold the Reset button and power the router on. Release the button when the system indicator starts blinking: it blinks for 5 seconds. Connect the PC to a LAN port of the router and open 192.168.1.1. The PC gets its address by itself.

263.text: Use BreedEnter: Athena answers it while the router boots and opens the web interface.

264.title: Web interface
264.text: Overview — model, CPU, RAM, flash memory, Athena version and build date. Update — writes a file to the chosen part: Firmware — the firmware update file; Athena bootloader — the file from the table above; Factory — EEPROM; Full image — a full dump of this very device, overwrites the whole flash memory. After writing, the router stays in the bootloader or reboots, as you choose. Reset — erases the firmware settings together with its internal storage: the firmware starts as on a new device. The firmware, the bootloader, U-Config and EEPROM stay. Reboot.

265.title: Recovery over TFTP
265.text: If the firmware does not start, Athena can download it from a TFTP server on the PC. The file name depends on the model: Model File name CMCC RAX3000M/Me cmcc-rax3000m-me_recovery.bin CMCC XR30 cmcc-xr30_recovery.bin Cudy RE3000 cudy-re3000_recovery.bin Cudy WBR3000UAX cudy-wbr3000uax_recovery.bin Cudy WR3000P cudy-wr3000p_recovery.bin Netis NX31 netis-nx-series_recovery.bin Netis NX32U netis-nxu-series_recovery.bin Xiaomi AX3000T xiaomi-ax3000t_recovery.bin Set the static address 192.168.1.2 (mask 255.255.255.0) on the network card of the PC. Start a TFTP server and put the firmware update file into its folder under the name from the table above, for example xiaomi-ax3000t_recovery.bin. Connect the PC to a LAN port, power off the router, hold the WPS (Mesh) button and power the router on. Release the button when the system indicator starts blinking. Athena downloads the file, writes it and reboots the router. Cudy TR3000 has no WPS button, so this recovery is not available on it: use the web interface.

290.title: There is no USB port speed switch
290.text: On models with USB 3.0 the switch may be missing from the web interface. To change the port mode, run the command in the CLI: To switch to USB 2.0: Enter one command at a time 1 system set dev.usb.force_usb2 1 2 system configuration save To switch to USB 3.0: Enter one command at a time 1 system set dev.usb.force_usb2 0 2 system configuration save 4

291.title: How do I add a device to Mesh?
291.text: Switch the device to repeater mode following the official guide, then capture it. Tip Mesh can be set up both with original routers and with clones. Make sure the devices have different service data — Mesh capture requires it. It is better to capture flashed devices over a cable. After a successful capture you can unplug it: the connection switches to Wi-Fi. If you run into problems, see the troubleshooting section. 5

292.title: Can I update with the official firmware?
292.text: No. A self-update may overwrite the bootloader, and the device will no longer start. Recovery will then require UART or a programmer. 6

293.title: The official bootloader is installed
293.text: Info If the official bootloader is installed and cannot be replaced the usual way: Download the NAND Breed rewrite file. In the running system, upload it as an update. After the reboot, enter Breed and upload the required files following the guide for your model. Tip If the router has no room for Entware or does not start, connect via TFTPD64 / UART and replace the bootloader. Tip On SmartBox Flash the stock bootloader expects the file name KN-1810_recovery.bin for TFTPD64 7

294.title: The system does not boot past Breed
294.text: Enter this command in Telnet: abstatus a) Autoboot command has been successfully executed / Firmware boot failed. The firmware was not written correctly. On devices with NAND memory use method #3. b) Autoboot was interrupted by button press. The Reset button was held during power-on. If nobody pressed it, roll back to another Breed version or use the version for another device. Boot and Recovery Environment for Embedded Devices Copyright (C) 2021 HackPascal <hackpascal@gmail.com> Build date 2021-12-16 [git-839fb85] Version 1.1 (r1338) Starting breed built-in shell breed> abstatus abstatus Autoboot command has been successfully executed / Firmware boot failed. c) If all partitions are written correctly but there are bad blocks, try booting the system from the other slot. To switch to the first slot, enter these commands in Telnet: Enter one command at a time 1 env set autoboot.command " boot flash 0x180000 " 2 env save To switch to the second slot, enter these commands in Telnet: Enter one command at a time 1 env set autoboot.command " boot flash 0x4140000 " 2 env save For devices with 256MB flash storage (SmartBox Pro, Xiaomi R3P) Enter one command at a time 1 env set autoboot.command " boot flash 0x8140000 " 2 env save 8

296.title: Starting the installer on macOS and Linux
296.text: macOS 12 or newer, on Apple silicon or Intel. The installer is not notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks the first launch: Open *_flasher from the archive and close the warning. Open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway next to the message about the installer, then confirm. On macOS 14 and older it is enough to Control-click the installer, choose Open and confirm. If macOS asks for access to a folder (Downloads, Desktop), allow it: backups are saved next to the installer. Linux on x86-64 with a graphical desktop. The installer is an AppImage: Allow it to run: in the file properties turn on Allow executing file as program, or run chmod +x *_flasher.AppImage. Start it. If it reports that no suitable fusermount was found, install the fuse3 package. Backups are saved next to the installer.

302.title: Glossary
302.text: Short explanations of words used in the guides. In the guides these words are underlined with dots — hover over them or tap them to see the explanation.

304.title: Breed
304.text: An alternative bootloader for routers with Broadcom and MediaTek processors. Its web interface or Telnet console is used to write the firmware, EEPROM and other partitions. More about Breed K

305.title: KeenBOOT
305.text: A proprietary bootloader for routers based on MediaTek MT7621 and MT7981 with a web interface: firmware installation, full dump, backups. More about KeenBOOT A

306.title: Athena
306.text: The Project Athens bootloader for routers based on MediaTek MT7981 with a web interface: writing the firmware and the bootloader, settings reset, full dump. More about Athena

308.title: EEPROM
308.text: A flash memory partition with the Wi-Fi calibration and the MAC address. Every router has its own: without the right EEPROM, Wi-Fi works poorly or not at all. You can extract it from a dump and set the MAC in the tools. U

309.title: U-Config
309.text: A partition with the device's service data: serial number, service tag, service password and region. A new U-Config can be generated in the tools. F

310.title: Full dump
310.text: A complete backup of the router's entire flash memory. With it, the device can be returned to its original state. O

311.title: OTA
311.text: An over-the-air update: the new version is downloaded and installed right on the router, without files on a computer. O

312.title: OpenWrt
312.text: An open Linux-based firmware for routers. On some models our firmware is installed from it.

314.title: KeenKit
314.text: A router maintenance script: firmware updates from a file and over OTA, partition and Entware backups. More about KeenKit E

315.title: Entware
315.text: A repository of extra software for the router. It is installed with the opkg package manager to the built-in memory or a USB drive. Installing Entware M

316.title: Mesh
316.text: Several routers combined into one Wi-Fi network with shared management. Mesh setup

318.title: BreedEnter
318.text: A Windows program that interrupts the system boot and opens the Breed bootloader without the Reset button. How to use it H

319.title: HFS
319.text: HTTP File Server — a simple Windows program that shares files over the network. Breed downloads firmware files from it with the wget command. P

320.title: PuTTY
320.text: A Windows program for connecting to the router's console over Telnet or SSH. T

321.title: TFTPD64
321.text: A TFTP server program for Windows. Some factory bootloaders download the firmware file through it during recovery.

323.title: Telnet
323.text: A text console protocol. It is used to enter commands in the Breed bootloader — strictly one at a time. S

324.title: SSH
324.text: A secure connection to the router's console: for example, to install Entware or run KeenKit. U

325.title: UART
325.text: A serial port on the router's board. With a USB-UART adapter you can control the bootloader even when the system does not start.

326.title: KeenBOOT
326.text: A proprietary bootloader for MediaTek MT7621 and MT7981. Advantages Improved bad block handling Web interface with file uploads Upload of a full device dump DHCP support without setting a static IP address Stopping the system boot with BreedEnter Dual-Image support for mipsel

329.title: Method I
329.text: Hold Reset and power on the router. Release the button after 10 seconds and open 192.168.1.1 from a device connected to a LAN port of the router. Older versions of the ARM bootloader may require the Mesh /WPS button and a static IP address to enter. Details

331.title: Switching from the Breed bootloader MT7621
331.text: Go to the Upgrade section, choose the file in the Bootloader field and click Upload.

332.title: Installing firmware MT7621
332.text: Use an incognito window in your browser. Format the flash memory if you are switching from another firmware (stock, custom and so on) or want a clean installation: in format, confirm that you saved a full image, type ERASE and click erase. In update, write the files for your model one by one, each to its partition: Firmware, RF-EEPROM and U-Config. Reboot the device.

333.title: Updating or changing the bootloader
333.text: Caution Do not update the bootloader if everything works. Go to update, choose the KeenBOOT (U-Boot) partition, select the bootloader file, turn on I understand the risk and click update.

334.title: KeenKit
334.text: A multi-purpose script that makes router maintenance easier. What the script can do Update firmware from file Finds a .bin file on the built-in or an external drive and installs it to the Firmware partitions. Partition backup Saves the selected partitions to the chosen drive. Entware backup Creates a full backup of the drive the script runs from. You can use it for a new installation. Replace partition Replaces a system partition with a file chosen by the user. OTA Update Online upgrade or downgrade of the firmware. Update service data Creates a new U-Config with updated service data and replaces the current one. KeenBOOT OTA Update Online upgrade or downgrade of the bootloader.

335.title: Installation
335.text: Install Entware. Connect to the router over SSH. Run the command: opkg update && opkg install curl && curl -L -s " https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spatiumstas/KeenKit/main/install.sh " > /tmp/install.sh && sh /tmp/install.sh OTA Update When KeenKit asks for the domain in OTA Update or KeenBOOT OTA Update, enter https://osvault.project-athens.com.

338.title: Adding a node over cable
338.text: In System Settings → General, click Change operating mode, choose Extender Mode and click Save. Connect the router to the controller with a cable. Caution! Since version 5.0.1, a device switched to Repeater mode may keep its login password. Remove it or reset the settings: Open the repeater's web interface. Remove the password through the CLI: user admin no pass Run the command on the controller. candidate is the repeater's MAC address; press Tab to fill it in automatically: mws revisit {candidate} In Wi-Fi System, click Acquire. Transferring the settings may take up to 2 minutes. When the capture succeeds, the router appears in the list with its serial number in the name, for example: Extender 943***359.

339.title: Adding a node wirelessly
339.text: In System Settings → General, click Change operating mode, choose Extender Mode and click Save. After the mode changes, connect to the router with a cable or over Wi-Fi. The web interface will be available at 192.168.1.3. To connect with a cable, set a static IP address on the network card. In the Wireless Connection section, connect to the controller's wireless network. Caution! Since version 5.0.1, a device switched to Repeater mode may keep its login password. Remove it or reset the settings: Open the repeater's web interface. Remove the password through the CLI: user admin no pass Run the command on the controller. candidate is the repeater's MAC address; press Tab to fill it in automatically: mws revisit {candidate} On the controller, open Wi-Fi System and click Acquire. Transferring the settings may take up to 2 minutes. When the capture succeeds, the router appears in the list with its serial number in the name, for example: Extender 943***359.

341.title: 1. The node is not captured
341.titles: Setting up a Mesh system › Troubleshooting
341.text: Make sure the devices you add have different serial numbers. It is shown on the home page in the About the system block. If the serial numbers match, use the U-Config generator or KeenKit with the Replace service data function. Using the U-Config generator: Open the U-Config tab Drag the U-Config from the firmware archive into the upload area or choose the file in the dialog. Download the generated file and flash it, or replace it with KeenKit. On devices with SPI memory you can load a full dump (Full) saved in Breed into the script and restore from it.

342.title: 2. Does not connect over the air after a wired capture
342.titles: Setting up a Mesh system › Troubleshooting
342.text: On the controller, turn on Backhaul Connection in Wi-Fi System → Settings.

343.title: 3. Error Mws::Controller::Candidate: "xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx": invalid CSR response
343.titles: Setting up a Mesh system › Troubleshooting
343.text: The error appears after capturing a device with the same service number and/or MAC address. To fix it, follow the steps from the first item.

344.title: 4. Error failed to connect: operation timeout
344.titles: Setting up a Mesh system › Troubleshooting
344.text: This is a normal message: the repeater is trying to reach the servers. It does not affect Mesh.

346.title: MediaTek MT7981 SPI NAND Flash
346.text: Find the full backup full_backup.bin.gz in the folder with the script: the installer created it before installing the firmware. Unpack it with an archiver such as 7-Zip to get full_backup.bin. If there is no full backup but you have backups of separate partitions, merge them with Merger or run this command in a terminal: copy /b mtd0.bin+mtd1.bin+mtd2.bin+mtd8.bin+mtd5.bin+mtd6.bin+mtd7.bin full_dump.bin For Xiaomi AX3000T the file will be 5.6 MB: it contains all partitions needed before flashing. Enter the Athena bootloader. Open Update, choose Full image and the backup file. Tick “I have checked the file and accept the risk”, choose Reboot the device and click Write and reboot. Warning On Xiaomi AX3000T, restore the device with the MiWiFi Repair Tool after the restart.

347.title: MediaTek MT7622 SPI NAND Flash
347.text: Using the files and steps from the recovery instructions, put the OpenWrt image into the folder, renaming the files to AX6S_recovery.bin and KN-1811_recovery.bin beforehand. After OpenWrt starts, upload the factory backups and write them to the flash memory. Commands Enter one command at a time 1 opkg update 2 opkg install kmod-mtd-rw 3 insmod mtd-rw i_want_a_brick= 1 4 cd /tmp/ 5 mtd unlock /dev/mtd2 6 mtd write /tmp/mtd3_uboot.bin u-boot 7 mtd unlock /dev/mtd3 8 mtd write /tmp/mtd4_Nvram.bin u-boot-env 9 mtd unlock /dev/mtd4 10 mtd write /tmp/mtd5_Bdata.bin bdata 11 mtd unlock /dev/mtd5 12 mtd write /tmp/mtd6_Factory.bin factory After the device reboots, use MIWIFIRepairTool to install the factory firmware.

349.title: Method I NAND Flash
349.text: Install KeenBOOT version 1.4 or later. In update, choose the Full image partition, select the backup file, turn on I understand the risk and click update. Upload the device backup. Caution! The full device backup must be exactly 128 MB (134,217,728 bytes). Tip If the router boots into Breed after the restore, install the factory bootloader for your model (see step 7 below). Archive of stock MT7621 bootloaders

350.title: Method II NAND Flash
350.text: Open the backup in HxD. Select the first block that contains the Breed bootloader and delete it. Save the resulting file. It must be exactly 127 MB (133,693,440 bytes). Enter the Breed bootloader (how?) at 192.168.1.1. Add the backup to HFS. In PuTTY, run the commands that erase the memory and write the backup. Enter one command at a time 1 wget http://192.168.1.2/full.bin 2 flash erase 0x80000 0x7f00000 3 flash write 0x80000 0x80001000 0x7f80000 Go to the Upgrade section, choose the factory bootloader file in the Bootloader field and click Upload.

351.title: Method III SPI NOR
351.text: Enter the Breed bootloader (how?) at 192.168.1.1. Upload a 16 or 32 MB backup, depending on the device's memory size. Go to the Upgrade section, choose the factory bootloader file in the Bootloader field and click Upload.

353.title: UART recovery
353.text: Download .zip If the router does not start and does not open the bootloader either, Athena can be started over UART. mtk_uartboot hands Athena to the BootROM of the router, Athena runs from memory and opens the web interface. Nothing is written to the flash memory until you write it yourself. You will need A USB-UART adapter with 3.3 V levels and its driver Access to the UART contacts on the board: the router has to be opened A network cable between the PC and a LAN port of the router

354.title: What's in the archive
354.text: Athena for UART, mtk_uartboot for Windows, macOS and Linux, BL2 for DDR3 and DDR4 memory and scripts that start it all. Athena for UART opens the web interface at every start and cannot be written to the flash memory.

355.title: Connecting
355.text: Power off the router and open it. Find the UART contacts on the board: GND, RX and TX. Connect GND to GND, TX of the adapter to RX of the router and RX of the adapter to TX of the router. Do not connect VCC. Plug the adapter into the PC and connect the PC to a LAN port of the router.

356.title: Starting Athena
356.text: Unpack the archive and start the script from its folder: Windows — start.bat; macOS — in the Terminal type sh, drag start.sh into the window and press Enter; Linux — sudo sh start.sh in the Terminal. The script asks the model of the router and finds the adapter by itself; if there are several serial ports, it asks which one is the adapter. When Handshake... appears, power the router on. mtk_uartboot sends BL2 and Athena and finishes after Received FIP. Wait about 5 seconds and open 192.168.1.1. The PC gets its address by itself. Athena for UART does not drive the LEDs of the router, except on Cudy RE3000 and TR3000: they do not show that it has started.

357.title: Repairing the router
357.text: Athena runs from memory with the usual web interface. In Update, write what is damaged: Athena bootloader — the bootloader of your model from the Athena page, not Athena_UART; Firmware — the firmware update file; Full image — a full dump of this very device. Then choose Reboot the device: the router starts from its flash memory again, mtk_uartboot is no longer needed.

358.title: If it does not work
358.text: Stays at Handshake... — TX and RX are swapped or GND is not connected. Power the router off, check the wires and power it on again: mtk_uartboot keeps waiting. An error while sending — the adapter does not keep up with the speed: try another one.

359.title: Updating firmware
359.text: Info You can also download the update file manually.

360.title: Official
360.text: For 5.0.7 and later Open System Settings → Files. In the firmware row, click the replace button and choose the update file. Confirm the update. The device will reboot.

361.title: Through the Athena bootloader MT7981
361.text: Enter the Athena bootloader. Open Update, keep Firmware and choose the update file. Choose Reboot the device and click Write and reboot.

363.title: Method I Recommended
363.text: Enter the KeenBOOT bootloader. In update, choose the Firmware partition, select the update file and click update.

364.title: Method II Automatic
364.text: Use KeenKit with the Update Firmware from File or OTA Update function.

365.title: Method III Via Breed
365.text: Caution A mistake in the commands may leave the router inoperable. Follow the instructions carefully. Enter Breed. Start PuTTY and connect over Telnet to 192.168.1.1 on port 23. Paste the commands one at a time with the right mouse button, waiting for each one to finish. Serve the firmware file with HFS.exe, for example under the name firmware.bin. Commands for devices with 256MB flash storage (SmartBox Pro, Xiaomi R3P) Run the commands one at a time, waiting for the previous one to finish. Enter one command at a time 1 flash erase 0x180000 0x1AB3F00 2 flash erase 0x8140000 0x1AB3F00 3 wget http://192.168.1.2/firmware.bin 4 flash write 0x180000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 5 flash write 0x8140000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 6 reset Commands for other devices Run the commands one at a time, waiting for the previous one to finish. Enter one command at a time 1 flash erase 0x180000 0x1AB3F00 2 flash erase 0x4140000 0x1AB3F00 3 wget http://192.168.1.2/firmware.bin 4 flash write 0x180000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 5 flash write 0x4140000 0x80001000 0x1AB3F00 6 reset

366.title: SPI NOR memory (up to 32MB)
366.text: Enter Breed. Open Upgrade → Generic → Firmware, choose the firmware file and upload it. The section names may differ depending on the Breed version. Note This section is for the firmware file only. Do not upload a full dump to it. After a successful upload the router reboots into the system.

367.title: Wiki
367.text: Ported firmware provides the basic functionality and supports most features of the original system, except for the vendor's cloud services. For evaluation only Ported firmware is an unofficial build. It is meant only for getting to know the system, not for everyday use. Do not use it on the listed routers as your main solution and do not install it on a device your internet connection or work depends on: failures, loss of settings and a bricked router are possible. All firmware, scripts and other files are provided “as is”, without warranty or technical support. Caution! Do not use the original firmware update files: this may leave the device inoperable. Do not contact official support or its chats about ported firmware. Doing so may get you banned from our chats. You bear full responsibility for the risks of flashing your device yourself. You can explore the range of original Keenetic products and find out where to buy them on the official website. Choose your model in the “Firmware” section of the side menu: each device page has the specifications, build features and a step-by-step installation guide.
